message.content: Lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) belong to two very different orders—Carnivora for the lion and Perissodactyla for the zebra. Their most recent common ancestor is therefore a mammal that lived before those two lineages split, roughly 60 million years ago. It would have been a small, insectivorous or omnivorous mammal that belonged to the clade **Laurasiatheria**, the group that gave rise to both Carnivora and Perissodactyla. In other words, the last common ancestor of lions and zebras was a small, early Laurasiatherian mammal that lived in the Paleogene period.
